newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: RTRS-Canberra moves Sydney airport flight paths.
newsitem.headline: RTRS-Canberra moves Sydney airport flight paths.

text.p: Australian Transport Minister John Sharp said the government had again changed flight paths to cut noise irritation from Sydney airport.

Sharp said he had directed that, subject to wind, early morning take-offs and landings would both fly -- in two-way traffic -- over the water to the south of the airport, thereby avoiding the houses to the north.

In a second change, aircraft taking-off to the north from Sydney's right-hand north-south runway would be required to turn right as soon as possible. Again, this would take them over water rather than over houses.

"This will allow the number of take-offs to the north from the main runway to be cut by up to half during those times when the airport is forced to operate in a northerly direction because of wind," Sharp said in a statement.
The two-way traffic early in the morning -- from 6 a.m. (2000 GMT) when the airport curfew ends to 7 a.m. -- was a safe and established practice at airports in other countries.
The procedure could not continue after 7 a.m. because it restricted the airport's capacity.
Sydney aircraft noise is a hot political topic, with residents even creating their own political party dedicated to shutting the airport.
After the new Liberal-National government gained power in March, Sharp implemented a promise to spread out air traffic above Sydney, sharing the noise among more residents.
The previous government had operated the airport under a fairly simple scheme of parallel approaches and departures from the two north-south runways.
The intersecting east-west runway was used only when winds demanded it.
But the new government recommenced operations on the cross runway while the other two were also in use.
